ideas.title: Measure and trim what each worker's claude -p loads at startup
ideas.problem: workers.run() starts claude -p with --system-prompt, --tools and --no-session-persistence (workers.py lines 87-94) but nothing else. Per the official headless docs, without --bare a -p run still loads everything an interactive session would, including anything in ~/.claude: auto memory, CLAUDE.md memory files, skills list, plugins, MCP servers and hooks. Our workers (Doulya, Sage, Vera, Serge, Calina, Israa, Tarek, Omar, Rana, Ghassan) run in empty folders on the owner's PC, where his own ~/.claude is full (this Builder chat, memory notes, skills). The repo has no CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY, DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS, --strict-mcp-config or --disable-slash-commands anywhere. We have never measured it: the usage table keeps input/output/cache tokens per run, so the baseline already exists. --bare itself is not an option: the docs say it never reads OAuth or the keychain, so our subscription login would fail.
ideas.proposal: Step 1 (free, no code): pick Vera (shortest run, $0.06). Run her once in practice-off mode as today, then once with the extra switches below set by hand, and compare input+cache tokens from the usage table (cp.usage_today). Step 2, only if the saving is 10%+ per run: in workers.run() add to the command `--strict-mcp-config` and `--disable-slash-commands`, and add to the env copy (atlas_engine._env() result) CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1. Put it behind a rule `workers.lean_start` (default on, in rules.py) so Atlas or the owner can switch it off. Do NOT touch Atlas's own claude -p in atlas_engine.py: he needs his journal and memory. Try `--setting-sources project,local` only if a local test shows the login still works (official docs list the flag; no source says what it does to OAuth). Watch for a case where Ghassan or Rana relied on a user-level skill: both get explicit tools, so none should.
ideas.gain: Fewer input and cache-write tokens on every one-shot worker run, which counts against the subscription allowances (SUBSCRIPTION_DAILY_VALUE_USD per agent). Size unknown: one blogger measured ~150k tokens before work in a repo with a long CLAUDE.md, skills and two MCP servers; ours is an empty folder, so the real saving may be small. That is why step 1 measures first. Success = per-run input+cache tokens down 10% or more for Vera, Serge and Israa with identical output quality.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: Vera on one idea, before and after, compare the usage rows; verdict JSON still valid. 2) Edge: Calina batch (WebSearch+WebFetch tools) still searches and writes episodes with sources. 3) Failure: with rule workers.lean_start on, a run where claude is signed in via the subscription still returns structured_output (no 'Not logged in'); if it fails, the rule goes off and the old command runs. Pass = same verdicts/episode counts and lower token rows.
ideas.confidence_why: The docs (tier A) say -p loads user config and name the switches; no measurement for our setup exists, and the OAuth interaction of --setting-sources is unverified. Weakest link: the saving may be tiny in an empty working folder.
ideas.risks: A switch might hide something a worker needs (user-level settings, proxy config). --bare and later a possible default of --bare for -p (docs: 'will become the default for -p in a future release') could break subscription logins regardless: separate watch item. No outside code involved.
